slides.say: A O B is a sector of a circle with center O and a radius of two centimeters. Based on this and the figure, what is the area of the shaded region, in square centimeters?
at: A O B is a sector

slides.say: The shaded region is the sector, minus the right triangle inside it. So shaded equals sector minus triangle. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, by estimating the choices, and then with a partial calculation.
Let's start with estimation, before any numbers. First we look at the pattern of the calculation, and ask, where is the pi?

The pi is in the sector. The sector is part of the circle, and the circle's area is pi r squared. The triangle has only straight sides, so its area has no pi. So sector minus triangle gives the pattern pi minus a number. The pi can come with a fraction, like pi over two. But it comes first, and a number is taken away from it.
at: The pi is in the sector
gives the pattern pi minus a number

slides.say: Choice number one says four minus pi. That's a number minus pi, the opposite pattern. Here the pi is the part taken away, so choice number one is out.
at: so choice number one is out

slides.say: Choice number three says pi over root two. That's pi divided by a number, and nothing is taken away. The triangle is missing, so choice number three is out too.
at: so choice number three is out too

slides.say: Choice number two says one half, times pi over two minus two. The half multiplies both parts, so it's pi over four, minus one. Choice number four says pi over two, minus one. Both have the pattern pi minus a number, so this test can't split them.

slides: Sometimes the pattern rules out three choices, and sometimes none. Here it ruled out two, in seconds. And it works only because we know which part has the pi: here, the sector.

slides.say: [pause] Two choices are left. Now let's estimate their size. Pi is a bit more than three, and less than four.
at: Pi is a bit more than three

slides.say: Look at choice number two. Inside the bracket, we have pi over two, minus two. Pi is less than four, so pi over two is less than four over two, which is two.
If we take two away from something less than two, we get a negative number. And half of a negative number is still negative. So choice number two is a negative number.
But an area can't be negative, so choice number two is out. The exam won't write minus five. It hides the minus behind the pi, and an estimate shows it at once.
at: But an area can't be negative
so choice number two is out

slides.say: Three choices are out, so choice number four is our answer.
at: so choice number four is our answer

slides.say: [pause] Now a second way, the math way, for whoever wants to calculate. Even then, we don't have to calculate everything. Let's find only the sector.
What part of the circle is the sector? Think of a pizza. If we cut it into four slices, each slice has ninety degrees. If we cut it into eight, each slice has forty-five degrees.
at: If we cut it into eight

slides.say: Our angle is forty-five degrees, so the sector is one of eight equal slices. It's one eighth of the circle.
The area of the circle is pi r squared. The radius is two, and two squared is four, so the circle is four pi. One eighth of four pi is four pi over eight, which is pi over two.

Now let's peek at the choices. Which of them has the sector, pi over two? Choice number four, pi over two minus one, has it. Choice number two has a half outside. The half multiplies the pi over two too, so it gives pi over four. That's not our sector, so choice number two is out.
at: so choice number two is out

slides.say: Choice number one has minus pi, and choice number three has pi over root two. Those two don't have pi over two at all. So the sector alone leaves only choice number four. To be sure, let's check the other piece, the triangle.

The triangle has a right angle and an angle of forty-five degrees. So its third angle is forty-five too, and its legs are equal. The hypotenuse is the radius, two. By Pythagoras, the two equal legs squared add up to four. So each leg squared is two.

The triangle's area is leg times leg, divided by two. The legs are equal, so leg times leg is a leg squared, two. Two divided by two is one. So the shaded area is pi over two minus one. That's exactly choice number four, our answer.
at: Two divided by two is one

slides.say: This is a partial calculation: find a useful piece, then look at the choices. Here the sector alone ruled out every choice but one. I'll see you in the next question.
